practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary distinction between tax evasion and tax avoidance?
opts: Tax evasion is legal, while tax avoidance is illegal.
Tax avoidance exploits legal loopholes to minimize tax, whereas tax evasion uses illegal means to conceal income.
Both tax evasion and tax avoidance are strictly criminal offences under international law.
Tax avoidance applies only to indirect taxes, while tax evasion applies to direct taxes.
practiceQuestions.sol: Tax avoidance involves minimizing tax liability by taking advantage of loopholes, ambiguities, or gaps in domestic and international tax laws, which is technically legal though ethically questionable. Tax evasion, conversely, involves illegal practices such as hiding income, inflating expenses, or failing to report earnings to escape tax obligations. [Primary Reference: Economic Survey and Income Tax Act, 1961 Context / Official UPSC GS-3 Syllabus Reference]

practiceQuestions.q: Under which section of the Income Tax Act, 1961, were the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) introduced in India?
opts: Section 80C
Section 90
Section 95 to 102
Section 144A
practiceQuestions.sol: The General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) provisions were inserted into the Income Tax Act, 1961, under Chapter X-A, spanning Sections 95 to 102, to counteract aggressive tax planning arrangements lacking commercial substance. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 / Union Budget Provisions]

practiceQuestions.q: What does the acronym 'BEPS', a major initiative by the OECD and G20 to curb international tax avoidance, stand for?
opts: Base Erosion and Profit Shifting
Border Enforcement and Protection Scheme
Business Equity and Partnership Standard
Balanced Economic Policy Strategy
practiceQuestions.sol: BEPS stands for Base Erosion and Profit Shifting. It refers to tax planning strategies used by multinational enterprises that exploit gaps and mismatches in tax rules to artificially shift profits to low or no-tax locations where there is little or no economic activity. [Primary Reference: OECD/G20 BEPS Project / Ministry of Finance Reports]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following treaties/agreements enables automatic exchange of financial account information (AEOI) globally to combat offshore tax evasion?
opts: Multilateral Competent Authority Agreement (MCAA) based on the Common Reporting Standard (CRS)
Kyoto Protocol on Climate Change
Basel III Accord on Banking Regulations
Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations
practiceQuestions.sol: The Common Reporting Standard (CRS), supported by the Multilateral Competent Authority Agreement (MCAA), facilitates the automatic exchange of financial account information between participating tax jurisdictions to detect and deter offshore tax evasion. [Primary Reference: CBDT / OECD Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of introducing the Place of Effective Management (POEM) guidelines in Indian tax law?
opts: To determine the residential status of foreign companies based on where key management decisions are made
To regulate foreign direct investment caps in multi-brand retail
To streamline Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration for domestic manufacturers
To set up special economic zones for export-oriented units
practiceQuestions.sol: POEM is used to determine the tax residency of a foreign company in India. If a foreign company's Place of Effective Management is found to be in India, its global income becomes taxable in India, preventing shell companies from claiming foreign status to avoid taxes. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 / CBDT Circulars on POEM]

practiceQuestions.q: Which bilateral tax agreement between India and a prominent European island nation was historically scrutinized and subsequently amended to plug treaty abuse and capital gains tax avoidance?
opts: India-Mauritius Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA)
India-Japan Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement
India-USA Bilateral Investment Treaty
India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement
practiceQuestions.sol: The India-Mauritius DTAA historically permitted residents of Mauritius routing investments into India to escape capital gains tax in India. The protocol amending the treaty in 2016 granted India source-based taxation rights on capital gains, curtailing rampant treaty shopping. [Primary Reference: Ministry of Finance / Protocol amending India-Mauritius DTAA]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary role of Transfer Pricing regulations under the Indian Income Tax Act?
opts: To regulate pricing of domestic retail commodities under consumer protection laws
To ensure that transactions between associated enterprises under common control are priced at arm's length price to prevent profit shifting
To fix freight and tariff rates for public sector shipping companies
To determine exchange rates for foreign institutional investments
practiceQuestions.sol: Transfer pricing regulations apply to international transactions and specified domestic transactions between associated enterprises. They mandate that prices charged in such related-party transactions must reflect the 'Arm's Length Price' (ALP)—what independent entities would charge—thereby preventing artificial profit shifting to low-tax jurisdictions. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Sections 92 to 92F]

practiceQuestions.q: Which reporting mechanism requires large multinational enterprises (MNEs) to provide an annual breakdown of revenue, profit, taxes paid, and economic activity per jurisdiction in which they operate?
opts: Country-by-Country Reporting (CbCR)
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Audit Return
Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) Statement
Goods and Services Tax Annual Return (GSTR-9)
practiceQuestions.sol: Country-by-Country Reporting (CbCR), part of BEPS Action 13, requires large MNEs with global revenues above a specified threshold to submit a detailed report providing aggregate tax and economic data for every country they operate in, aiding tax authorities in assessing high-level transfer pricing risks. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 / OECD BEPS Action 13]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary purpose of introducing Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) in India's tax administration?
opts: To provide upfront certainty on transfer pricing methodologies for international transactions
To fast-track bankruptcy resolution for corporate debtors
To grant tax holidays to start-ups in tier-2 cities
To subsidize agricultural equipment imports
practiceQuestions.sol: Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) entered into between the CBDT and taxpayers provide certainty regarding the transfer pricing methodology to be applied to international transactions for future years, reducing litigation and aggressive tax avoidance disputes. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Sections 92CC and 92CD]

practiceQuestions.q: Which international instrument, signed by India, aims to swiftly implement BEPS tax treaty-related measures without bilateral renegotiations?
opts: Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (MLI)
Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer
Rotterdam Convention on Prior Informed Consent Procedure
Minamata Convention on Mercury
practiceQuestions.sol: The Multilateral Instrument (MLI) allows countries to modify their existing bilateral tax treaties (DTAAs) expeditiously to incorporate BEPS anti-abuse measures (such as the Principal Purpose Test) without having to renegotiate each treaty bilaterally. [Primary Reference: OECD BEPS Action 15 / Ministry of Finance Notifications]

practiceQuestions.q: How does the 'Principal Purpose Test' (PPT) incorporated under tax treaties and the MLI function as a bulwark against treaty shopping?
opts: It denies treaty benefits if obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction, unless it is established that granting the benefit accords with the object and purpose of the provisions.
It automatically imposes a flat 40% withholding tax on all cross-border dividend payments regardless of tax treaties.
It restricts foreign institutional investors from trading in Indian government securities without prior RBI clearance.
It requires all multinational companies to list their Indian subsidiaries on domestic stock exchanges within two years.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Principal Purpose Test (PPT) is a general anti-abuse rule under BEPS Action 6. It denies a tax treaty benefit if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of the arrangement or transaction, safeguarding against treaty abuse (treaty shopping). [Primary Reference: OECD BEPS Action 6 / MLI Article 7]

practiceQuestions.q: Why are hybrid mismatch arrangements frequently exploited for tax avoidance, and how do international tax reforms address them?
opts: They exploit differences in the legal characterization of financial instruments or entities across two jurisdictions, leading to double non-taxation or deduction without inclusion.
They combine domestic and foreign indirect taxes into a single consolidated tax credit scheme.
They allow companies to evade customs duties by rerouting cargo through land-locked neighboring countries.
They merge corporate income tax with personal income tax for promoters holding majority shares.
practiceQuestions.sol: Hybrid mismatch arrangements exploit differences in tax laws between countries (e.g., treating an instrument as debt in one country and equity in another). This results in deductions in both jurisdictions or a deduction in one without taxation in the other. BEPS Action 2 recommendations and domestic anti-hybrid rules neutralize these mismatches by denying deductions or including payments in income. [Primary Reference: OECD BEPS Action 2 / Income Tax Act Amendments]

practiceQuestions.q: How does India's domestic General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) interact with bilateral Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs)?
opts: DTAA provisions override GAAR provisions in all circumstances without exception.
GAAR provisions can override DTAA benefits if an arrangement is declared an 'impermissible avoidance arrangement', as explicitly provided under the Income Tax Act.
GAAR is applicable exclusively to domestic entities and has no legal standing against foreign treaty residents.
GAAR can only be invoked with the prior unanimous approval of the United Nations Tax Committee.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Section 90(2A) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, the provisions of Chapter X-A (GAAR) shall apply even if they are inconsistent with the provisions of a DTAA. This statutory override ensures that aggressive tax avoidance cannot be shielded merely by routing through a treaty partner jurisdiction. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Section 90(2A) and Chapter X-A]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary significance of the 'Equalisation Levy' introduced by India in recent years?
opts: To tax digital transactions and e-commerce supply chains of foreign non-resident digital service providers lacking a physical permanent establishment in India.
To equalize freight charges across public and private railways for bulk commodity transportation.
To subsidize digital literacy programs in rural educational institutions.
To levy tariffs on agricultural imports from developed nations to protect domestic farmers.
practiceQuestions.sol: Introduced via the Finance Act (and later expanded), the Equalisation Levy aims to capture tax revenue from digital advertising, online services, and e-commerce supplies provided by non-resident entities that generate substantial revenue in India without maintaining a physical Permanent Establishment (PE), bypassing traditional nexus-based taxation. [Primary Reference: Finance Act / Income Tax Act Provisions on Equalisation Levy]

practiceQuestions.q: How do 'Safe Harbour' rules in Indian Transfer Pricing regulations operate to reduce tax litigation?
opts: They allow taxpayers to accept transfer pricing margins pre-determined by tax authorities, guaranteeing exemption from detailed transfer pricing audits and scrutiny.
They provide tax havens for corporate entities within coastal special economic zones.
They exempt foreign portfolio investors from capital gains tax if investments are held in safe banking sectors.
They grant immunity from criminal prosecution for individuals who voluntarily disclose undisclosed foreign assets.
practiceQuestions.sol: Safe Harbour rules refer to circumstances in which the tax authorities shall accept the transfer pricing price declared by the taxpayer as given. By agreeing to predefined mark-ups or margins, taxpayers avoid protracted audits, transfer pricing adjustments, and litigation. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Section 92CB]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the strategic significance of the 'Multilateral Competent Authority Agreement' (MCAA) signed by India under the Automatic Exchange of Information (AEOI) framework?
opts: It establishes a single procedural framework to operationalize bilateral and multilateral data exchanges of offshore bank accounts without needing separate negotiations with each country.
It standardizes interest rates on foreign currency non-resident deposits across global commercial banks.
It creates a joint military task force to seize assets of fugitive economic offenders hiding in foreign jurisdictions.
It merges customs clearance procedures for all landlocked South Asian nations.
practiceQuestions.sol: The MCAA operationalizes the Common Reporting Standard (CRS). Instead of negotiating hundreds of bilateral tax information exchange agreements (TIEAs), India uses the MCAA to automatically receive financial account data from over 100 jurisdictions, piercing through foreign bank secrecy. [Primary Reference: CBDT / OECD Global Forum Framework]

practiceQuestions.q: How do domestic withholding tax (TDS/TCS) provisions act as an anti-tax avoidance and revenue augmentation mechanism in India?
opts: By collecting tax at the very source of income generation, ensuring regular cash flow to the exchequer and discouraging cash-based concealment of earnings.
By imposing penalties directly on corporate boards for failing to meet export quotas.
By replacing all corporate income taxes with a single flat transaction tax on bank withdrawals.
By providing interest-free loans to taxpayers who file returns ahead of schedule.
practiceQuestions.sol: Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) and Tax Collected at Source (TCS) mechanisms ensure that the government collects tax at the point where income is credited or paid, rather than waiting for the end of the financial year. This broadens the tax net, generates steady advance revenue, and creates an audit trail that deters tax evasion. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Chapter XVII]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the core rationale behind introducing the 'Faceless Assessment' and 'Faceless Appeal' schemes in India's direct tax administration?
opts: To eliminate physical interface between taxpayers and tax officers, thereby curbing corruption, bias, and arbitrary tax avoidance scrutiny decisions.
To replace human tax auditors entirely with artificial intelligence algorithms that assess tax slabs without legal oversight.
To enable anonymous shell companies to register for tax identification numbers without submitting physical documents.
To decentralize tax collection down to village panchayats for localized audit management.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Faceless Assessment and Appeal system utilizes randomized allocation of cases across the country using technology, ensuring complete anonymity between the assessing officer and the taxpayer. This transparency reduces discretionary powers, curtails corruption, and ensures uniform, objective application of anti-avoidance measures. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Sections 143(3A), (3B), (3C) & CBDT Guidelines]

practiceQuestions.q: How do domestic anti-abuse provisions regarding 'Secondary Adjustments' under Transfer Pricing function in India?
opts: They require the excess money resulting from a primary transfer pricing adjustment to be repatriated to India, or treated as an advance loan carrying imputed interest.
They impose a secondary penalty tax on domestic suppliers who fail to file GST returns on time.
They allow companies to adjust past tax liabilities against future carbon credit earnings.
They permit foreign parent companies to write off Indian subsidiary losses against global tax credits.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Section 92CE of the Income Tax Act, a secondary adjustment is required when a primary transfer pricing adjustment increases a taxpayer's taxable income. Since the actual cash often remains with the foreign associated enterprise, secondary adjustments ensure that the excess money is repatriated to India within a stipulated time, preventing wealth from being parked abroad outside the tax net. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Section 92CE]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary role of the 'Financial Intelligence Unit - India' (FIU-IND) in countering tax evasion and aggressive avoidance?
opts: To receive, process, analyze, and disseminate information relating to suspect financial transactions to domestic and international enforcement agencies.
To formulate monetary policy interest rates and manage foreign exchange reserves.
To audit the expenditure of central government ministries and public sector undertakings.
To negotiate bilateral free trade agreements with developing economies.
practiceQuestions.sol: FIU-IND is the central national agency responsible for receiving, processing, analyzing, and disseminating information relating to suspect financial transactions under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), playing a crucial role in tracking untaxed wealth and aggressive tax evasion networks. [Primary Reference: Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) / Ministry of Finance Notifications]

practiceQuestions.q:

1. GAAR provisions can be invoked to declare an arrangement an 'impermissible avoidance arrangement' if its main purpose is to obtain a tax benefit.
2. The approval of a Panel headed by a High Court judge is mandatory before GAAR can be invoked by the tax authorities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: GAAR empowers tax authorities to declare an arrangement as an 'impermissible avoidance arrangement' if the main purpose is to obtain a tax benefit and it lacks commercial substance. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Approving Panel for GAAR consists of a Chairperson who is a judge of a High Court, along with other members, but the review process requires following specific institutional safeguards (not necessarily a panel headed exclusively by a High Court judge in all administrative review stages without specific statutory composition—actually the Approving Panel is headed by a High Court judge, but let's check exact composition: yes, the Approving Panel is chaired by a judge of a High Court. Wait, both statements are factually accurate under the Income Tax Act! Let's check statement 2: Under Section 96/99/144BA, reference to the Approving Panel (headed by a High Court judge) is mandatory before invoking GAAR. Therefore, both 1 and 2 are correct. Let's make C the correct answer for Q21 in the final payload.) [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Sections 95-102]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) Actions:
1. Action 6 of BEPS relates to the prevention of tax treaty abuse, including the introduction of the Principal Purpose Test (PPT).
2. Action 13 introduces standardized Country-by-Country Reporting (CbCR) for multinational enterprises.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. BEPS Action 6 specifically targets treaty abuse through anti-abuse rules like the Principal Purpose Test. BEPS Action 13 establishes the three-tiered transfer pricing documentation standard, which includes the Master File, Local File, and Country-by-Country Reporting (CbCR). [Primary Reference: OECD/G20 BEPS Project Actions 6 and 13]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Place of Effective Management (POEM) guidelines in India:
1. POEM is used to determine whether a foreign company has a permanent establishment in India for indirect tax purposes.
2. For the purpose of POEM, the 'active business outside India' (ABOI) test is used to exempt companies that conduct the majority of their economic operations abroad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because POEM determines corporate *residence* for *direct tax* (income tax) purposes, not indirect tax or permanent establishment status. Statement 2 is correct: the ABOI test exempts foreign companies from POEM scrutiny in India if their passive income is below a threshold and active business is predominantly conducted outside India. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Section 6(3) & CBDT Guidelines on POEM]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Transfer Pricing regulations in India:
1. Transfer pricing regulations apply exclusively to international transactions between foreign parent companies and Indian subsidiaries.
2. Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) can be entered into for a maximum period of 5 future years, with a provision for rollback for up to 4 preceding years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Indian transfer pricing regulations apply not only to international transactions between associated enterprises but also to specified domestic transactions (SDTs) between domestic entities under certain conditions. Statement 2 is correct: APAs can be valid for up to 5 consecutive future years and include a rollback mechanism for up to 4 preceding years. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Sections 92, 92CC, 92CD]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the automatic exchange of financial information (AEOI):
1. India receives financial account information under the Common Reporting Standard (CRS) developed by the OECD and G20.
2. The Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) is a bilateral agreement between India and the United States to combat offshore tax evasion by US persons in India and Indian persons in the US.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. India is an early adopter of the Common Reporting Standard (CRS) for multilateral AEOI. Additionally, India signed an Inter-Governmental Agreement (IGA) with the United States to implement FATCA, enabling mutual exchange of financial account data to curb offshore tax evasion. [Primary Reference: CBDT / Inter-Governmental Agreement between India and USA on FATCA]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Multilateral Instrument (MLI) to implement BEPS measures:
1. India has ratified the MLI to modify its bilateral tax treaties without requiring individual renegotiations.
2. The MLI overrides all provisions of bilateral DTAAs automatically without regard to the reservations and notifications made by signatory countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: India ratified the MLI to swiftly implement BEPS tax treaty measures across its network of DTAAs. Statement 2 is incorrect because the MLI operates flexibly, modifying treaties only where both contracting jurisdictions have matched their choices, and it respects the specific reservations and notifications made by each country under the MLI framework. [Primary Reference: OECD BEPS Action 15 / Ministry of Finance Notifications on MLI]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the taxation of indirect transfer of assets (often associated with the retrospective tax controversy):
1. Section 9 of the Income Tax Act was amended retrospectively to tax capital gains arising from the transfer of shares of a foreign company deriving its value substantially from assets located in India.
2. The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 effectively nullified all retrospective tax demands related to indirect asset transfers prior to May 28, 2012, subject to the withdrawal of pending litigation by taxpayers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Statement 1 reflects the retrospective legislative amendment following the Supreme Court's Vodafone ruling to tax indirect transfers. Statement 2 reflects the 2021 legislative amendment that dropped all retrospective tax demands prior to May 2012 provided taxpayers withdrew ongoing litigation and agreed not to claim damages, resolving long-standing tax disputes. [Primary Reference: Income Tax Act, 1961 - Section 9 & Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015:
1. It was enacted specifically to deal with unaccounted foreign income and assets held abroad by Indian residents, providing for stringent penalties and prosecution.
2. The Act provides a domestic tax amnesty window that allows foreign asset holders to regularize their assets without any financial penalty or tax liability.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Black Money Act, 2015 was enacted to penalize undisclosed foreign assets and income with a flat 30% tax plus heavy penalties and rigorous imprisonment. Statement 2 is incorrect because while the Act initially offered a limited compliance window, it required payment of tax (30%) and penalty (30%), totaling 60%, rather than zero tax or penalty. [Primary Reference: Black Money Act, 2015 / Ministry of Finance Notifications]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the amendment to the India-Mauritius Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) in 2016:
1. It introduced source-based taxation of capital gains on shares acquired by Mauritian residents in Indian companies.
2. It abolished all withholding taxes on interest and royalty payments between India and Mauritius unconditionally.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The 2016 protocol amended the India-Mauritius DTAA giving India the right to tax capital gains on shares of Indian resident companies sold by Mauritian residents, phasing it in over a transition period. Statement 2 is incorrect because withholding taxes on interest and royalties were not abolished unconditionally under the protocol. [Primary Reference: Protocol amending India-Mauritius DTAA, 2016]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the OECD/G20 Two-Pillar Solution to address the tax challenges arising from the digitalization of the economy:
1. Pillar One seeks to reallocate a portion of taxing rights over large multinational enterprises to market jurisdictions where consumers and users are located, regardless of physical presence.
2. Pillar Two introduces a global minimum corporate tax rate of 15% to stop profit shifting to low-tax jurisdictions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework Two-Pillar solution addresses digitalization tax challenges: Pillar One reallocates profits to market jurisdictions where users/consumers reside (addressing the nexus issue), while Pillar Two establishes a global minimum corporate tax rate of 15% to eliminate tax competition and profit shifting. [Primary Reference: OECD/G20 Two-Pillar Solution / Ministry of Finance Context]
